title: Input symbol after repeated walks
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean input symbols, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$. For any direction flag $neg$, Boolean flag $bl$, and natural number $a$, after $a$ repetitions of the simulated input-head walk in direction $neg$, the scanned input symbol equals the symbol of $x$ at the original input-head position shifted by $-a$ when $neg$ is true and by $a$ otherwise, with positions outside $x$ read as blank.
hypotheses_covered: M is a finite-state Turing machine over Boolean symbols
c is a configuration of M on x
neg and bl are Boolean flags
